expected_output.reasoning: The investigation correctly identifies the core root cause described in the expectation: one task (pool-b, a separate pool registered in the same target group perf-demo-07-catalog-tg) runs with an index-refresh hold (INDEX_REFRESH_HOLD_MS=280) that blocks/delays requests, causing ~25% of traffic through the shared target group to be slow (~188ms avg vs ~50ms for healthy tasks), while the ALB keeps round-robining a full share to it. The investigation traces this to the CloudFormation parameter PoolBIndexRefreshHoldMillis=280 on pool-b vs 0 on the main catalog service, matching the expected root cause of a divergent task definition config with an index-refresh hold causing lock-based delays on one of the four targets. It also correctly notes this affects ~25% of requests and explains the afternoon pattern as load-driven surfacing of an always-present per-task issue (consistent with the expected note that the afternoon rate step is the trigger, not the cause). Minor differences: the investigation doesn't explicitly mention 'lock' terminology or the exact p50/p90/p99 numbers, and attributes the s7redesign2 baseline latency increase as a separate hypothesis rather than fully folding it in, but the key identifying details (service, parameter, task, target group, percentage of traffic, divergent config) match closely enough to constitute the same root cause identification.
